evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Institute of History and Philology Museum
evidence.field: Explanation of oracle-bone 年 and divination text
evidence.text: The museum interprets oracle-bone 年 as 禾 above 人, depicting a person bearing grain, and explains the Shang paired questions 我受年 / 我不其受年 as asking whether there would be a good harvest. This supports an early Shang harvest use, but does not establish that it was the character’s first use.
evidence.kind: institutional paleographic account with transcribed inscription
evidence.title: 我受年──甲骨文「年」的故事

evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Center for Digital Cultures / Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 字形演變; explanation of early structure and lower-element change
evidence.text: The entry calls harvest 年’s original meaning, describes oracle-bone and bronze forms as 禾 above 人, and reports that the lower 人 in small-seal forms changed into 千. This records the database’s graphic-history account; the sequence was not independently checked against a dated run of inspected glyph images.
evidence.title: 漢字「年」：字形演變

evidence.field: 年、歲、祀 in an oracle-bone inscription; disputed sound analysis
evidence.text: The article analyzes oracle-bone 年 as grain-related in meaning and proposes that the lower 人 also supplies sound, while citing the traditional Shuowen analysis 禾 plus phonetic 千. It discusses a Shang-period inscription distinguishing 年 as harvest, 歲 as harvest season, and 祀 as the regnal-year count. These are the article’s interpretations; its inspected text gives no reconstruction to evaluate the proposed phonetic relationship.
evidence.title: 漢字の来た道｜漢字文化資料館

evidence.field: Character-specific kMandarin lookup attempts for U+4EBA and U+5E74
evidence.text: The official character-specific Unihan pages for 人 and 年 could not be opened in the browser. The supplied local rows give 人 = rén and 年 = nián; these are current readings and do not establish an ancient sound relationship.
evidence.kind: access failure and local-row provenance note
evidence.title: Unihan Data Lookup (U+4EBA; U+5E74)

evidence.text: Supplied local rows: 人 = rén; 年 = nián. The external character-specific Unicode records could not be inspected. This pair is included as a current Mandarin comparison only, not as evidence of a historical phonetic role.

evidence.title: Unihan Data Lookup (U+4EBA; U+5E74)

evidence.field: sources/baxter-sagart/baxtersagart.tsv, exact 人 and 年 rows supplied as local_primary_readings
evidence.text: Supplied Baxter–Sagart 2014 rows: 人, MC nyin, OC *ni[ŋ]; 年, MC nen, OC *C.nˤi[ŋ]. These values preserve the local table’s notation and are not externally verified here. They do not by themselves establish that 人 was phonetic in the earliest 年 graph.
evidence.title: Baxter–Sagart 2014 table rows (local dataset)

search_audit.query: site:museum.sinica.edu.tw/en/knowledge-base/item/30 年 我受年 harvest oracle bone; 年 商代 甲骨文 受年 禾 人 字形 harvest meaning museum; Unicode Unihan U+4EBA U+5E74 kMandarin
search_audit.outcome: Search returned institutional and scholarly character accounts. Opened the Academia Sinica museum, Academia Sinica character database, and Taishukan pages and inspected their contents. Both exact Unicode Unihan record URLs were inaccessible; the general Unihan search page opened but did not verify either character’s row.

gaps: The museum supports an early Shang harvest use, not that this is 年’s earliest use overall.

Whether 人 had a phonetic role in early 年 remains disputed. The local modern readings 人 rén and 年 nián, and the supplied Baxter–Sagart rows, do not settle the issue; no externally inspectable official Unihan character rows were available.
The reported lower-element change from 人 to 千 and the Shuowen analysis 禾千聲 were not independently checked against a dated sequence of inspected glyph forms.

items.period: Shang dynasty; oracle-bone script style, modern vector rendering of a Xiaoxuetang glyph identified as 42.F100, 甲2827 合27941
items.caption: An oracle-bone form of 年, rendered with 禾 above a human-shaped element. It illustrates the museum’s early harvest interpretation; the form alone does not establish whether 人 also supplied sound.
items.alt: Black oracle-bone-style graph on white: a branching grain-like upper form above a separate human-shaped lower form.
items.selection_reason: The exact file description identifies this 年 form and attributes it to a specific Xiaoxuetang record. It provides a sourced example of the form used to explain the grain-and-person interpretation.
items.rights: The Commons description states CC0 1.0 for the Xiaoxuetang glyph image and public-domain status for the modern vector representation. Modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

limitations.text: The selected rendering is a modern redraw. The pictorial account is supported by the museum, but the lower element’s possible phonetic role remains disputed; this research did not independently inspect a dated series of glyph images.
